You are the Niyam encoder. Update this rulebook so it matches a new government document.

The validated change set is in `.niyam/changeset.json`. It lists each change with its exact source quote, page and clause.
The source document is registered in `sources/index.yaml` as `gr-202407031335114330` (date 2024-07-03).

Do this:
1. Read CLAUDE.md (the rulebook rules), the change set, and the files of the affected scheme(s): mh.ladki_bahin.
2. Apply every change in the change set, following CLAUDE.md exactly:
   - parameter change: add a new dated value under `values:` starting 2024-07-03. Never edit or delete older values.
   - condition change: set `valid_until` on the old condition to the day before 2024-07-03, and add a new condition with the same id and `valid_from: 2024-07-03`.
   - condition removed: only set `valid_until` to the day before 2024-07-03.
   - every new value or condition gets `source` / `metadata.reference` with doc `gr-202407031335114330`, page, clause, quote (copied from the change set) and quote_en.
   - if a change needs a new person field, add it to `schema/person.yaml` with a safe default that keeps existing results unchanged.
3. Add test citizens to `tests/` for every change, dated on or after 2024-07-03: just below, at, and just above each limit, plus one case dated before 2024-07-03 proving the old rule still applies. Each case cites `GR 202407031335114330 p.<page> clause <clause>` in `source`.
4. Add an entry at the top of CHANGELOG.md (English, Hindi, Marathi) linking to the document.
5. Run `python -m niyam_rulebook test` and fix problems until it prints `0 failed` with no PROBLEM lines.
6. Do not run git. Do not edit files outside schemes/, parameters/, tests/, sources/, glossary/, schema/ and CHANGELOG.md.

Finish with a short summary of what you changed and the final test result.

## Amendments to Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana (GR dated 3 July 2024)

- English: From 3 July 2024 the maximum age rises from 60 to 65. One unmarried woman per family can now apply. Families with contract, outsourced or volunteer workers are no longer disqualified (regular employees and pensioners still are). A woman who already gets Rs 1,500 or more a month from other government schemes is now not eligible (before, only more than Rs 1,500 disqualified her). The limit on family farm land (five acres) is removed.
- हिंदी: 3 जुलाई 2024 से अधिकतम आयु 60 से बढ़कर 65 वर्ष हो गई है। हर परिवार की एक अविवाहित महिला भी आवेदन कर सकती है। संविदा, बाह्य एजेंसी या स्वयंसेवी कर्मचारी वाले परिवार अब अपात्र नहीं होंगे (नियमित कर्मचारी और पेंशनधारी अब भी अपात्र हैं)। जो महिला अन्य सरकारी योजनाओं से पहले से 1,500 रुपये या अधिक प्रतिमाह पा रही है, वह अब पात्र नहीं है (पहले केवल 1,500 रुपये से अधिक पर अपात्र थी)। परिवार की पाँच एकड़ कृषि भूमि की सीमा हटा दी गई है।
- मराठी: 3 जुलै 2024 पासून कमाल वय 60 वरून 65 वर्षे झाले आहे. प्रत्येक कुटुंबातील एक अविवाहित महिलाही अर्ज करू शकते. कंत्राटी, बाह्य यंत्रणेतील किंवा स्वयंसेवी कामगार असलेली कुटुंबे आता अपात्र ठरणार नाहीत (नियमित कर्मचारी आणि निवृत्तीवेतनधारक अजूनही अपात्र आहेत). इतर सरकारी योजनांमधून दरमहा 1,500 रुपये किंवा अधिक लाभ घेणारी महिला आता पात्र नाही (पूर्वी फक्त 1,500 रुपयांपेक्षा जास्त असल्यास अपात्र होती). कुटुंबाच्या पाच एकर शेतजमिनीची मर्यादा काढून टाकली आहे.
- Source: [GR 202407031335114330](https://gr.maharashtra.gov.in/Site/Upload/Government%20Resolutions/Marathi/202407031335114330.pdf)

content.text:
I applied all six changes from GR 202407031335114330, and `python -m niyam_rulebook test` prints `45 passed, 0 failed` with no PROBLEM lines.

**Parameters** (new values dated 2024-07-03, older values untouched, each with the GR reference):
- **c1:** `age_max` goes from 60 to 65.
- **c2:** `eligible_marital_statuses` now includes `unmarried`.
- **c4:** `disqualifying_govt_jobs` is now `[regular, pensioner]`.

**Conditions** in `schemes/mh/ladki_bahin.yaml`:
- **c5:** The old `other_scheme_limit` now ends 2024-07-02. A new one from 2024-07-03 uses `<`, so receiving exactly Rs 1,500 disqualifies.
- **c6:** `farm_land_limit` only gets `valid_until: 2024-07-02`.
- **c3:** The new `one_unmarried_per_family` condition applies only to unmarried women: `marital_status != 'unmarried' or not other_unmarried_beneficiary_in_family`. The change set's bare `not person.other_unmarried_beneficiary_in_family` would also have disqualified married women with that flag set. The clause says only one unmarried woman per family, so I scoped it.

**Schema:** `schema/person.yaml` already had `other_unmarried_beneficiary_in_family` with a default of false, so I didn't change it.

**Tests:** I added 21 cases. Each change has cases dated on or after 2024-07-03 around its limit, plus one dated 2024-07-02 showing the old rule. For example, age 64, 65 and 66, and Rs 1,499, 1,500 and 1,501 from other schemes. The farm land cases are 5, 5.5 and 20 acres, since there is no limit left to test around. Every case cites `GR 202407031335114330 p.2 clause <clause>`.

**CHANGELOG.md:** A new entry at the top in English, Hindi and Marathi, linking to the GR.

I didn't model the two ambiguities in the change set: whether the Rs 2.5 lakh limit for contract workers is personal or family income, and what the ration-card income exemption covers. I left the existing income ceiling as it was. I did not run git.
